summary.text: Mike Rogers is a former U.S. Army officer and FBI special agent who served in the Michigan Senate and then in the U.S. House for Michigan's 8th District from 2001 to 2015, where he chaired the House Intelligence Committee. After leaving Congress he worked in cybersecurity and media. He was the Republican nominee for Senate in 2024, losing narrowly to Elissa Slotkin, and is the 2026 Republican nominee.

paragraphs.text: Born June 2, 1963; his family settled in Brighton Township, and he graduated from Howell High School (Wikipedia says 1981). Ballotpedia and Wikipedia differ on his birthplace (Livingston County and Livonia, respectively).
Earned a B.S. from Adrian College in 1985 (Wikipedia says in criminal justice and sociology).
Served in the U.S. Army from 1985 to 1989.
Worked as an FBI special agent in the Chicago field office from 1989 to 1994, specializing in organized crime and public corruption.

Elected to the Michigan Senate in 1994 and re-elected in 1998, representing District 26 (Clinton, Livingston and Shiawassee counties); he was the primary sponsor of the law creating the Michigan Education Savings Program.
Won Michigan's 8th Congressional District in 2000 by 111 votes over Democratic state Sen. Dianne Byrum and served until 2015, announcing in March 2014 that he would not seek an eighth term.

In the House, served on the Energy and Commerce Committee and chaired the Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence from 2011 to 2015; he introduced the Cyber Intelligence Sharing and Protection Act in 2011.

After Congress, worked in the cybersecurity industry, joined CNN as a national security commentator and hosted radio and television programs; he served on the Mitre Corporation board from 2016 to 2023, as chairman from 2021.
Announced a 2024 Senate run in August 2023, won that Republican primary, and lost the general election to Elissa Slotkin by fewer than 20,000 votes.
Announced his 2026 Senate candidacy on April 14, 2025, and won the August 4, 2026 Republican primary unopposed.
